Structuring Data: Transforming from Start to End dates to Wide Format

```{r}
#setwd("~/Research/Politics/Risk Pool/R Files/")

#Loading in the raw data for lower officeholders.
riskpoolraw.df <- read_csv(here::here("data", "RiskPoolData.csv"))
  # read.csv("RiskPoolData.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#Loading in identifiers for roles held
rolenames <- read_csv(here::here("data","RoleNames.csv"))

#Loading in the candidates for higher office
candidate.df <- read_csv(here::here("data","CandidateData.csv"))

#Loading in the Gallup Opinion data
opinions.df <- read_csv(here::here("data", "Polls.csv"))
```

```{r}
#Converting the raw officeholder variables into their proper format
##riskpoolraw.df$Name <- gsub("\n\n", "", riskpoolraw.df$Name, fixed = TRUE)
riskpoolraw.df$Name <- str_replace_all(riskpoolraw.df$Name,"\n\n", "")
riskpoolraw.df$CandOneState <- paste(riskpoolraw.df$Name, riskpoolraw.df$State)
riskpoolraw.df$Start <- as.numeric(riskpoolraw.df$Start)
riskpoolraw.df$End <- as.numeric(riskpoolraw.df$End)
riskpoolraw.df$BirthYear <- as.numeric(riskpoolraw.df$BirthYear)
riskpoolraw.df$EarlyBird <- as.numeric(riskpoolraw.df$EarlyBird)
riskpoolraw.df$LameDuck[is.na(riskpoolraw.df$LameDuck)] <- 0
riskpoolraw.df$LameDuck[is.na(riskpoolraw.df$EarlyBird)] <- 0
```

```{r}
#Removing officeholder raw data that do not reflect legitimate officeholder observations and observations of officeholders that did not serve during our observation period
riskpoolraw.df <- riskpoolraw.df[!is.na(riskpoolraw.df$Start),]
riskpoolraw.df <- riskpoolraw.df[riskpoolraw.df$Start != 0,]
riskpoolraw.df <- riskpoolraw.df[riskpoolraw.df$End != 0,]
riskpoolraw.df <- riskpoolraw.df[!is.na(riskpoolraw.df$Start),]
riskpoolraw.df <- riskpoolraw.df[!is.na(riskpoolraw.df$End),]

riskpoolraw.df <- riskpoolraw.df[riskpoolraw.df$End > 1890,]
riskpoolraw.df <- riskpoolraw.df[riskpoolraw.df$Start != 2018,]
riskpoolraw.df$End[riskpoolraw.df$End > 2017] <-2017

#Making pre-1891 start dates equal to 1891 to allow for processing
riskpoolraw.df$Start[riskpoolraw.df$Start < 1891] <- 1891

#The raw data includes start and end years of officeholders. Additionally, it may include multiple rows for the same officeholder (e.g., if held discontinous terms, held multiple offices). For our analysis, we want a long dataset - a single row for each officeholder-year. For ease of processing, we first build a wide dataset, with one row for each officeholder and a column for each year in our dataset. We begin converting the dataset by creating columns for each year in the observation period and determining if a risk pool member served in that year. Later, we will convert this wide dataset into a long dataset.

#For each candidate, we observe their start year and end year and use that to populate their columns for years served.
#If it's their first year in office / last year in office and they are an early bird / lame duck, we append that notation to their office name
for(a in 1:nrow(riskpoolraw.df)){
  numberYears <- riskpoolraw.df$End[a] - riskpoolraw.df$Start[a]
  inoffceyear <-  match(paste("InOffice",riskpoolraw.df$End[a], sep = ""), colnames(riskpoolraw.df))
  
  if (riskpoolraw.df$LameDuck[a] == 1) {
    riskpoolraw.df[a,inoffceyear] <- paste(riskpoolraw.df$Office[a], "LameDuck")
    }else{ 
  riskpoolraw.df[a,inoffceyear] <- riskpoolraw.df$Office[a]
    }
  
  if (numberYears == 0) {
  }else{
  for (b in 1:numberYears) {
    if (b == numberYears & riskpoolraw.df$EarlyBird[a] == 1){
      inoffceyear <-  match(paste("InOffice",riskpoolraw.df$End[a], sep = ""), colnames(riskpoolraw.df)) - b
    riskpoolraw.df[a,inoffceyear] <- paste(riskpoolraw.df$Office[a], "EarlyBird")
    }else{
    inoffceyear <-  match(paste("InOffice",riskpoolraw.df$End[a], sep = ""), colnames(riskpoolraw.df)) - b
    riskpoolraw.df[a,inoffceyear] <- riskpoolraw.df$Office[a]
    }
    }
  }
}
```

```{r}
#To account for the possibility that we have multiple rows for the same officeholder, we need to create a new dataframe that collapses across equivalent officeholder names. We identify unique officeholders by their name and state. For our collapsed output, we create a data frame that includes a single row for each unique officeholder.
riskpool.df <- as.data.frame(unique(riskpoolraw.df$CandOneState))
colnames(riskpool.df) <- c("CandOneState")

#Then, we add in the Name, Party, State, Gender, and Minority Status of these officeholders
# NOTE THAT MINORITY STATUS ONLY APPLIES TO HOUSE MEMBERS, NOT THE OTHER THREE RISK POOL OFFICES (since we did not collect it for the other three offices, all of them just say "0", and our analyses with minority status are only done on the subset of House members, not the full sample)
for(c in 1:nrow(riskpool.df)){
riskpool.df$CandOneName[c] <- unique(riskpoolraw.df$Name[riskpoolraw.df$CandOneState == riskpool.df$CandOneState[c]])
riskpool.df$Gender[c] <- unique(riskpoolraw.df$Gender[riskpoolraw.df$CandOneState == riskpool.df$CandOneState[c]])
riskpool.df$State[c] <- unique(riskpoolraw.df$State[riskpoolraw.df$CandOneState == riskpool.df$CandOneState[c]])
riskpool.df$BirthYear[c] <- unique(riskpoolraw.df$BirthYear[riskpoolraw.df$CandOneState == riskpool.df$CandOneState[c]])
riskpool.df$isMinority[c] <- unique(riskpoolraw.df$isMinority[riskpoolraw.df$CandOneState == riskpool.df$CandOneState[c]])
  }

#Finally, we add the office held in each year for each unique name-state
```

Structuring Data: Converting Wide Format to Long Format

```{r}
#We need to convert the wide dataset into a long dataset. We begin by creating the initial columns of the long dataset and then populating the rows with wide dataset's data. We measure since 1891 to account for pre-1920 experience.
riskpoollong.df <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = nrow(riskpool.df)*(2017-1890), ncol = 11))
colnames(riskpoollong.df) <- c("NameNorm", "State", "NameNormState", "Gender", "isMinority", "Year", "InOffice", "BirthYear")

for(a in 1:(2017-1890)){
  riskpoollong.df$NameNorm[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- riskpool.df$NameNorm
  riskpoollong.df$State[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- riskpool.df$State
  riskpoollong.df$NameNormState[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- riskpool.df$NameNormState
  riskpoollong.df$Gender[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- riskpool.df$Gender
  riskpoollong.df$isMinority[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- riskpool.df$isMinority
  riskpoollong.df$Year[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- 1890+a
  riskpoollong.df$InOffice[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- 
          riskpool.df[,match(paste("InOffice",riskpoollong.df$Year[(1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df))], sep = ""), colnames(riskpool.df))]
  riskpoollong.df$BirthYear[c((1+(a-1)*nrow(riskpool.df)):(a*nrow(riskpool.df)))] <- riskpool.df$BirthYear
}

#Standardizing State and Office Names
riskpoollong.df$StateNoSpace <- gsub(" ", "", riskpoollong.df$State)
riskpoollong.df$InOffice <- gsub("_", "", riskpoollong.df$InOffice)

#Creating a list of ways offices were coded to use as matches to indicate if a candidate held each specific office
LtGovlist <- rolenames$LtGov[nchar(rolenames$LtGov) >0]
Houselist <- rolenames$House[nchar(rolenames$House) >0]
SecStatelist <- rolenames$SecState[nchar(rolenames$SecState) >0]
AGlist <- rolenames$AttorneyGeneral[nchar(rolenames$AttorneyGeneral) >0]
MultOfficeEBorLD <- rolenames$MultipleOfficesAndEBorLD[nchar(rolenames$MultipleOfficesAndEBorLD) >0]

#If held multiple offices and one of those offices was tagged as a lame duck or early bird, delete out the lame duck / early bird office (the non-lame duck / non-early bird office will be considered their office for that year). Because Lame Duck / Early Bird indication always comes after the name of the office that was a lame duck / early bird, can find that way.
riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD <- as.numeric(riskpoollong.df$InOffice %in% MultOfficeEBorLD)
riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1] <- gsub("Secretary of State LameDuck", "", riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1])
riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1] <- gsub("LtGov LameDuck", "", riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1])
riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1] <- gsub("Attorney General LameDuck", "", riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1])
riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1] <- gsub("Secretary of State EarlyBird", "", riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1])
riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1] <- gsub("LtGov EarlyBird", "", riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1])
riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1] <- gsub("Attorney General EarlyBird", "", riskpoollong.df$InOffice[riskpoollong.df$isMultOfficeEBorLD == 1])

#If held only one office in a year and had early bird / lame duck designation, identify whether they were a lame duck / early bird and code appropriately. Can then remove lame duck / early bird tag in office name to properly then code their office.
riskpoollong.df$EarlyBird <- 0
riskpoollong.df$LameDuck <- 0
riskpoollong.df$EarlyBird <- as.numeric(regexpr("EarlyBird", riskpoollong.df$InOffice) > 0)
riskpoollong.df$LameDuck <- as.numeric(regexpr("LameDuck", riskpoollong.df$InOffice) > 0)
riskpoollong.df$InOffice <- gsub("EarlyBird","",riskpoollong.df$InOffice)
riskpoollong.df$InOffice <- gsub("LameDuck","",riskpoollong.df$InOffice)
riskpoollong.df$InOffice <- trimws(riskpoollong.df$InOffice, which = "both")

#Creating columns for each risk pool office served and determining whether the role held matches one of the recognized office titles
riskpoollong.df$isLtGov <- as.numeric(riskpoollong.df$InOffice %in% LtGovlist)
riskpoollong.df$isHouse <- as.numeric(riskpoollong.df$InOffice %in% Houselist)
riskpoollong.df$isSecState <- as.numeric(riskpoollong.df$InOffice %in% SecStatelist)
riskpoollong.df$isAG <- as.numeric(riskpoollong.df$InOffice %in% AGlist)
riskpoollong.df$InPool <- as.numeric(riskpoollong.df$InOffice != 0 & riskpoollong.df$InOffice != "")

#Creating a single column for the office the officeholder served in in the given year
riskpoollong.df$office[riskpoollong.df$InOffice == ""] <- ""
riskpoollong.df$office[riskpoollong.df$isAG == 1] <- "AttorneyGeneral"
riskpoollong.df$office[riskpoollong.df$isHouse == 1] <- "House"
riskpoollong.df$office[riskpoollong.df$isSecState == 1] <- "SecretaryOfState"
riskpoollong.df$office[riskpoollong.df$isLtGov == 1] <- "LieutenantGovernor"

      #Collecting descriptives
      numberHouse <- length(unique(riskpoollong.df$NameNormState[riskpoollong.df$isHouse == 1]))
      numberLtGov <- length(unique(riskpoollong.df$NameNormState[riskpoollong.df$isLtGov == 1]))
      numberAG <- length(unique(riskpoollong.df$NameNormState[riskpoollong.df$isAG == 1]))
      numberSecState <- length(unique(riskpoollong.df$NameNormState[riskpoollong.df$isSecState == 1]))
      
      
#Creating a data frame that only includes candidate-years where the member was in a risk pool office
riskpoollong.df.rem <- riskpoollong.df[riskpoollong.df$InPool == 1,]
riskpoollong.df.rem <- riskpoollong.df.rem[order(riskpoollong.df.rem$Year, decreasing = FALSE),]

#Because our lame duck /early bird coding was algorithmic, it may mis-identify some terms. One-year terms in office that are coded as a lame duck or early bird need to corrected to non-lame duck / non-early bird
riskpoollong.df.rem$OnlyYearEBorLD <- 0

for (x in 1:nrow(riskpoollong.df.rem)) {
  EarlyBirdButNotInPoolNextYear <- 0 
  #If they are an early bird
  EarlyBirdButNotInPoolNextYear <- as.numeric((riskpoollong.df.rem$EarlyBird[x] == 1) + 
  #And they are in the dataset in the subsequent year but in a different role
     sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] & 
           riskpoollong.df.rem$Year == (riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]+1) & 
           riskpoollong.df.rem$office != riskpoollong.df.rem$office[x]) +
  #Or they are not in the dataset in the subsequent year
         (nrow(riskpoollong.df.rem[(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] & 
           riskpoollong.df.rem$Year == (riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]+1)),]) == 0) == 2)
  #Then their early bird year should count as a normal year in office
  
  LameDuckButNotInPoolPriorYear <- 0
  #If they are a lame duck
  LameDuckButNotInPoolPriorYear <- as.numeric((riskpoollong.df.rem$LameDuck[x] == 1) +
  #And they are in the dataset in the previous year but in a different role
     sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] &
           riskpoollong.df.rem$Year == (riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]-1) & 
           riskpoollong.df.rem$office != riskpoollong.df.rem$office[x]) +
  #Or they are not in the dataset in the previous year
  (nrow(riskpoollong.df.rem[(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] & 
           riskpoollong.df.rem$Year == (riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]-1)),]) == 0) == 2)
  #Then their lame duck year should count as a normal year in office  
  
  riskpoollong.df.rem$OnlyYearEBorLD[x]  <- EarlyBirdButNotInPoolNextYear + LameDuckButNotInPoolPriorYear
}

#If we found that their only year in office was an early bird / lame duck, we remove the early bird / lame duck designation
riskpoollong.df.rem$LameDuck[riskpoollong.df.rem$OnlyYearEBorLD == 1] <- 0
riskpoollong.df.rem$EarlyBird[riskpoollong.df.rem$OnlyYearEBorLD == 1] <- 0


#Determing the offices a candidate held and number of years in office prior to the given year in the long data set since 1890
riskpoollong.df.rem$WasAG <- 0
riskpoollong.df.rem$WasHouse <- 0
riskpoollong.df.rem$WasSecState <- 0
riskpoollong.df.rem$WasLtGov <- 0

for (x in 1:nrow(riskpoollong.df.rem)) {
  riskpoollong.df.rem$WasAG[x] <- as.numeric(sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] & 
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$isAG == 1 &
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$Year < riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]) > 0) 
                                      
  riskpoollong.df.rem$WasHouse[x] <- as.numeric(sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] & 
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$isHouse == 1 &
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$Year < riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]) > 0) 
  
  riskpoollong.df.rem$WasSecState[x] <- as.numeric(sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] & 
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$isSecState == 1 &
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$Year < riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]) > 0) 

  riskpoollong.df.rem$WasLtGov[x] <- as.numeric(sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] & 
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$isLtGov == 1 &
                                      riskpoollong.df.rem$Year < riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]) > 0) 
}

riskpoollong.df.rem$TotalYearsOfService <- 0

#Calculating total experience inclusive and exclusive of early bird / lame duck years. First year in office is coded as 1 year.
for (x in 1:nrow(riskpoollong.df.rem)) {
  riskpoollong.df.rem$TotalYearsOfService[x] <- length(unique(riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[
                                              riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] &
                                              riskpoollong.df.rem$Year <= riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x]]))
  
  riskpoollong.df.rem$TotalYearsOfServiceNoEBLD[x] <- length(unique(riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[
                                              riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState == riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNormState[x] &
                                              riskpoollong.df.rem$Year <= riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x] & 
                                                riskpoollong.df.rem$LameDuck == 0 & riskpoollong.df.rem$EarlyBird == 0]))
    }

numberEarlyBirds <- sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$EarlyBird == 1)
numberLameDucks <- sum(riskpoollong.df.rem$LameDuck == 1)
```


Combining Data: Merging Risk Pool Data with Candidate Data

```{r}
#Reformatting the candidate.df dataframe
candidate.df$Candidate <- as.character(candidate.df$Candidate)
candidate.df$State <- as.character(candidate.df$State)
candidate.df$StateNoSpace <- gsub(" ", "", candidate.df$State)

#First, identify if a race ocurred in a risk pool member's state/year
for (x in 1:nrow(riskpoollong.df.rem)) {
  riskpoollong.df.rem$GovEventOccurred[x] <- sum(candidate.df$Year == riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x] &
                                                           candidate.df$StateNoSpace == riskpoollong.df.rem$StateNoSpace[x] &
                                                             candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 1)
  riskpoollong.df.rem$SenEventOccurred[x] <- sum(candidate.df$Year == riskpoollong.df.rem$Year[x] &
                                                             candidate.df$StateNoSpace == riskpoollong.df.rem$StateNoSpace[x] &
                                                             candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0)
}

riskpoollong.df.rem$AnyEventOccurred <- riskpoollong.df.rem$GovEventOccurred + riskpoollong.df.rem$SenEventOccurred

#Remove observations where no event ocurred
riskpoollong.df.rem <- riskpoollong.df.rem[riskpoollong.df.rem$AnyEventOccurred > 0,]

#Make candidate names consistent across databases
riskpoollong.df.rem$CandNameOneNorm <- gsub(" ", "", riskpoollong.df.rem$NameNorm)
riskpoollong.df.rem$CandNameOneNorm <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", riskpoollong.df.rem$CandNameOneNorm)

candidate.df$CandidateNorm <- gsub(" ", "", candidate.df$Candidate)
candidate.df$CandidateNorm <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", candidate.df$CandidateNorm)
candidate.df$Type <- as.character(candidate.df$Type)
candidate.df$Female1Male0 <- as.numeric(candidate.df$Female1Male0)

#Identify what kind of event it was, whether the candidate ran, if they were the incumbent, and if they won the race

#Split the dataframes to make it easier to identify specific events in the candidates dataset
senlongriskpool.df <- riskpoollong.df.rem[riskpoollong.df.rem$SenEventOccurred > 0,]
govlongriskpool.df <- riskpoollong.df.rem[riskpoollong.df.rem$GovEventOccurred > 0,]


#Create dataframes for our Sen and Gov data
sen.df <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = 100000, ncol = 26))
gov.df <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = 100000, ncol = 26))

colnames(sen.df) <- c("Name","State", "NameState", "Gender", "isMinority", "Year","TypeOfEvent","GovEvent1SenEvent0","isLtGov","isHouse","isSecState", "isAG",
                      "WasHouse", "WasAG", "WasLtGov","WasSecState", "EarlyBird", "LameDuck", "TotalYearsService",  "TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD",
                      "BirthYear", "WouldBeAgainstIncumbent", "WasCandidate", "Incumbent", "AgainstIncumbent", "Won")
colnames(gov.df) <-c("Name","State", "NameState", "Gender", "isMinority", "Year","TypeOfEvent","GovEvent1SenEvent0","isLtGov","isHouse","isSecState", "isAG",
                      "WasHouse", "WasAG", "WasLtGov","WasSecState", "EarlyBird", "LameDuck", "TotalYearsService",  "TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD",
                      "BirthYear", "WouldBeAgainstIncumbent", "WasCandidate", "Incumbent", "AgainstIncumbent", "Won")

#Creating unique RaceID and Event Type.  Will use the count of the unique RaceIDs to determine number of events.  Can define
#event type by deleting out the RaceID from it.
candidate.df$RaceIDType <- paste(candidate.df$RaceID, candidate.df$Type)

r <- 0
#For the Senate
for(y in 1:nrow(senlongriskpool.df)){
  numberOfSenEventsForOfficeInYear <- length(unique(candidate.df$RaceIDType[candidate.df$Year == senlongriskpool.df$Year[y] &
                                         candidate.df$StateNoSpace == senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y] &
                                         candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0]))
  typeOfSenEvents <- unique(candidate.df$RaceIDType[candidate.df$Year == senlongriskpool.df$Year[y] &
                                         candidate.df$StateNoSpace == senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y] &
                                         candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0])
  for(w in 1:numberOfSenEventsForOfficeInYear){
    r <- r+1
    sen.df$Name[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$NameNorm[y]
    sen.df$State[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y]
    sen.df$NameState[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$NameNormState[y]
    sen.df$Gender[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$Gender[y]
    sen.df$isMinority[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$isMinority[y]
    sen.df$Year[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$Year[y]
    sen.df$TypeOfEvent[r] <- trimws(substr(typeOfSenEvents[w], 
                                    nchar(unique(candidate.df$RaceID[candidate.df$RaceIDType == typeOfSenEvents[w]]))+1,100))
    sen.df$GovEvent1SenEvent0[r] <- 0
    sen.df$isLtGov[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$isLtGov[y]
    sen.df$isHouse[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$isHouse[y]
    sen.df$isSecState[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$isSecState[y]
    sen.df$isAG[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$isAG[y]
    sen.df$WasLtGov[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$WasLtGov[y]
    sen.df$WasHouse[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$WasHouse[y]
    sen.df$WasSecState[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$WasSecState[y]
    sen.df$WasAG[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$WasAG[y]
    sen.df$EarlyBird[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$EarlyBird[y]
    sen.df$LameDuck[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$LameDuck[y]
    sen.df$TotalYearsService[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$TotalYearsOfService[y]
    sen.df$TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$TotalYearsOfServiceNoEBLD[y]
    sen.df$BirthYear[r] <- senlongriskpool.df$BirthYear[y]
    sen.df$WouldBeAgainstIncumbent[r] <- sum(candidate.df$Year == senlongriskpool.df$Year[y] &
                                        candidate.df$StateNoSpace == senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y] &
                                        candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0 & candidate.df$RaceIDType == typeOfSenEvents[w] &
                                        candidate.df$Incumbent == 1 & 
                                          candidate.df$CandidateNorm != senlongriskpool.df$CandNameOneNorm[y])
    sen.df$WasCandidate[r] <- sum(candidate.df$Year == senlongriskpool.df$Year[y] &
                             candidate.df$StateNoSpace == senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y] &
                             candidate.df$CandidateNorm == senlongriskpool.df$CandNameOneNorm[y] &
                             candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0 & candidate.df$RaceIDType == typeOfSenEvents[w])
    sen.df$Incumbent[r] <- sum(candidate.df$Year == senlongriskpool.df$Year[y] &
                                   candidate.df$StateNoSpace == senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y] &
                                   candidate.df$CandidateNorm == senlongriskpool.df$CandNameOneNorm[y] &
                                   candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0 & candidate.df$RaceIDType == typeOfSenEvents[w] &
                                   candidate.df$Incumbent == 1)
    sen.df$AgainstIncumbent[r] <- sum(candidate.df$Year == senlongriskpool.df$Year[y] &
                                   candidate.df$StateNoSpace == senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y] &
                                   candidate.df$CandidateNorm == senlongriskpool.df$CandNameOneNorm[y] &
                                   candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0 & candidate.df$RaceIDType == typeOfSenEvents[w] &
                                   candidate.df$RunningAgainstIncumbent == 1)
    sen.df$Won[r] <- sum(candidate.df$Year == senlongriskpool.df$Year[y] &
                                   candidate.df$StateNoSpace == senlongriskpool.df$StateNoSpace[y] &
                                   candidate.df$CandidateNorm == senlongriskpool.df$CandNameOneNorm[y] &
                                   candidate.df$Gov1Sen0 == 0 & candidate.df$RaceIDType == typeOfSenEvents[w] &
                                   candidate.df$Won == 1)
}
}
```

```{r}

# This set of code restructures the data so that there is only one observation per person-year, and to filter out anyone with prior runs for higher office


# Below, we are creating a dataset that we can use to grab the individual-year specific variables (that is, not variables that differ for each election event). So, we are removing all duplicates based on NameState and Year (i.e., simply keeping the first one that appears in the dataset), for merging by NameState and Year with the "test" dataset which will have the election event-specific variables.
sengov.df.main.unique <- sengov.df.main %>%
  distinct(NameState, Year, .keep_all = TRUE)


# Next, we want to restructure the variables that differ for each election event - essentially, we want to create summary variables for each individual-year observation in case there were multiple elections for that individual-year. So the below is to create a dataframe with only one row IF there are multiple elections in a given year, to indicate whether the individual was a candidate in ANY election that year, how many total opportunities occurred that year, whether there were Governor and/or Senate events that year, and how many total incumbents there were. 
test <- sengov.df.main %>% 
  group_by(NameState, Year) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(WasCandidateEither = max(WasCandidate, na.rm = TRUE),
            NumberOpportunities = n(),
            GovEvent = max(GovernorEvent, na.rm = TRUE),
            SenEvent = max(SenateEvent, na.rm = TRUE),
            # This gets the total number of incumbents across all possible governor and senate races. Note that we want the total incumbents (not simply a binary variable) since we want to know how many of the total races that year had incumbents.
            TotalIncumbents = sum(GovernorIncumbent) + sum(SenateIncumbent), na.rm = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(Year, NameState)
# Merge to get the other variables that should be the same across each person-year, from the non-duplicated dataset created above
merged_test <- sengov.df.main.unique %>% 
  right_join(test, by = c("NameState" = "NameState", "Year" = "Year")) %>%
  # Now we can select only the variables needed for the main analysis. The dataset contains other variables that aren't needed, or that no longer make sense based on the way we restructured the data, so to avoid confusion, we remove them here. 
  dplyr::select(Name, State, NameState, Gender, isMinority, Year, TypeOfEvent, isLtGov, isHouse, isSecState, isAG, WasHouse, WasAG, WasLtGov, WasSecState, TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD, BirthYear, WasCandidate, Opinion, Age, Age.sq, even1odd0, TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD_log, GovernorEvent, SenateEvent, WasCandidateEither, NumberOpportunities, GovEvent, SenEvent, TotalIncumbents, PriorRuns)


# Remove instances of second runs given our focus on likelihood of running among first-time candidates.
merged_test_first_only <- merged_test %>%
  filter(PriorRuns == 0)
# Create experience squared variable
merged_test_first_only$TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD_sq <- merged_test_first_only$TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD^2


# There was one value erroneously entered for a male's age (the year was entered by accident) - fixing that here to just be an NA
merged_test_first_only$Age[!is.na(merged_test_first_only$Age) & 
                             merged_test_first_only$Gender == 0] <- NA
```

```{r}
# MAIN MODEL - Discrete model, including experience squared
discrete_model_quad <- glm.cluster(WasCandidateEither ~ Gender*TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD_sq +
                                     Gender*TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD +
                                isLtGov + isAG + isSecState + 
                         WasHouse + WasLtGov + WasAG + WasSecState + SenEvent 
                    + TotalIncumbents + NumberOpportunities + Year +
                         as.factor(State), cluster = 'Name',
                     data = merged_test_first_only, 
                     family = "binomial"(link = "cloglog"))
summary(discrete_model_quad)
# Get r-squared
r2_nagelkerke(discrete_model_quad$glm_res)
```

# Quintile Analysis and Plot (Figure 2 in Paper)

```{r}
# Quintiles with BINARY indicators for each quintile (dropping first quintile) - NO CONTROLS
quintile_breaks <- quantile(merged_test_first_only$TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD, probs = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2))
merged_test_first_only$quintile_exper2 <- as.numeric(cut(merged_test_first_only$TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD,
                                                        breaks = quintile_breaks, labels = FALSE, 
                                                        include.lowest = TRUE))
# Show values of quintile breaks
quintile_breaks

# Creating separate indicator variables for each quintile
for (i in 1:5) {
  merged_test_first_only[paste0("quintile_", i)] <- ifelse(merged_test_first_only$quintile_exper2 == i, 1, 0)
}

binary_quintile_model <- glm.cluster(WasCandidateEither ~ Gender*quintile_2 + Gender*quintile_3 +
                                       Gender*quintile_4 + Gender*quintile_5, cluster = 'Name',
                     data = merged_test_first_only, 
                     family = "binomial"(link = "cloglog"))
summary(binary_quintile_model)

# Plot with BINARY quintile variables
intercepteffect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)[1]
gendereffect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)[2]
# Assigning coefficients for each quintile and interaction
q2_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["quintile_2"]
q3_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["quintile_3"]
q4_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["quintile_4"]
q5_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["quintile_5"]
gender_q2_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["Gender:quintile_2"]
gender_q3_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["Gender:quintile_3"]
gender_q4_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["Gender:quintile_4"]
gender_q5_effect <- coef(binary_quintile_model)["Gender:quintile_5"]



predictedprobs <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = 10, ncol = 3))
colnames(predictedprobs) <- c("Female1Male0", "Tenure", "LikelihoodOfRunning")
predictedprobs$Female1Male0[1:5] <- 1
predictedprobs$Female1Male0[6:10] <- 0
predictedprobs$Tenure[1:5] <- 1:5
predictedprobs$Tenure[6:10] <- 1:5

predictedprobs$LikelihoodOfRunning <- intercepteffect +
  predictedprobs$Female1Male0 * gendereffect +
  ifelse(predictedprobs$Tenure == 2, q2_effect + predictedprobs$Female1Male0 * gender_q2_effect, 0) +
  ifelse(predictedprobs$Tenure == 3, q3_effect + predictedprobs$Female1Male0 * gender_q3_effect, 0) +
  ifelse(predictedprobs$Tenure == 4, q4_effect + predictedprobs$Female1Male0 * gender_q4_effect, 0) +
  ifelse(predictedprobs$Tenure == 5, q5_effect + predictedprobs$Female1Male0 * gender_q5_effect, 0)

predictedprobs$ProbabilityOfRunning <- 1 - exp(-exp(predictedprobs$LikelihoodOfRunning))
predictedprobs$PercentRunning <- 100 * predictedprobs$ProbabilityOfRunning


#Figure two plot
predictedprobs$Female0Male1 <- as.factor(1-as.numeric(predictedprobs$Female1Male0))
predictedprobs$Female1Male0 <- as.character(predictedprobs$Female1Male0)

# The following code generates the plot in a separate PDF file (this was used for submission for the proofs)
#pdf("wald_figure2.pdf", width = 10, height = 7)

ggplot(data = predictedprobs, aes(x = Tenure, y = PercentRunning, group = Female0Male1)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = Female0Male1), size = 1) + 
  geom_point(aes(shape = Female0Male1), size = 3) +  
  scale_linetype_manual(labels = c("Female", "Male"), values = c("solid", "dotted")) +
  scale_shape_manual(labels = c("Female", "Male"), values = c(16, 17), guide = FALSE) + 
  guides(linetype=guide_legend("Gender")) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Quintile of Experience", limits = c(1, 5), breaks = c(1,2,3,4,5)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Predicted Probability of Running \n (Percent)", limits = c(0,7)) +

  theme(axis.line = element_line(size = 1), axis.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")) +
```

# Derivatives Tests


```{r}
# Steps for derivative analyses
# 1. Manually compute derivatives at each value of gender and experience using the coefficient on experience, the coefficient on experience^2, AND IF FEMALE: the coefficient on the gender*experience interaction term, and 2 times the coefficient on the gender*experiences^2 interaction term. (Can write a function to compute these by plugging each value in.)
# 2. Manually compute the standard error of each linear combination of coefficients on gender*experience and gender*experience^2, at each value of experience (will need this for the t-test to test if different from zero). Formula is as follows: Var(aX + bY) = a^2 * Var(X) + b^2 * Var(Y) + 2ab * Cov(X,Y). Will thus need the covariance between X and Y (extract from covariance matrix). Plug in the value of experience as part of b (i.e., b should equal 2 * years).
# 3. Manually calculate the t-statistic: [combination of coefficients] / SE(combination of coefficients)
# 4. Manually determine the corresponding p-value (use R package for this).
```

```{r}
# STEP 1

# Saving main model again here to get coefficients
discrete_model_quad <- glm.cluster(WasCandidateEither ~ Gender*TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD_sq +
                                     Gender*TotalYearsServiceNoEBLD + isLtGov + isAG + isSecState + 
                       WasHouse + WasLtGov + WasAG + WasSecState + SenEvent 
                    + TotalIncumbents + NumberOpportunities + Year +
                         as.factor(State), cluster = 'Name',
                     data = merged_test_first_only,
                     family = "binomial"(link = "cloglog"))


tenureeffect <- coef(discrete_model_quad)[4]
tenure.sq.effect <- coef(discrete_model_quad)[3]
genderxtenureeffect <- coef(discrete_model_quad)[66] 
genderxtenure.sq.effect <- coef(discrete_model_quad)[65] 


derivative_values <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = 40, ncol = 3))
colnames(derivative_values) <- c("Female1Male0", "Tenure", "Derivative")
derivative_values$Female1Male0[1:20] <- 1
derivative_values$Female1Male0[21:40] <- 0
derivative_values$Tenure[1:20] <- 1:20
derivative_values$Tenure[21:40] <- 1:20


derivative_values$Derivative <- round(tenureeffect + 2 * tenure.sq.effect * derivative_values$Tenure + 
  genderxtenureeffect * derivative_values$Female1Male0 +
  2 * genderxtenure.sq.effect * derivative_values$Female1Male0 * derivative_values$Tenure,2)

derivative_values
```

```{r}
# STEP 2

# Obtain the covariance matrix of parameter estimates, which I will need to compute the SE of both coefficients jointly
# We are specifically interested in seeing whether the coefficient on gender * experience plus 2 * coefficient on gender * experience^2 is different from zero, so need the covariance for these two coefficients

# The below is checking the full matrix to double-check I am grabbing the right entry:
#options(max.print = 5000)
#vcov(discrete_model_quad)

# Set up the data frame to contain the eventual t-values, and the standard error values at each level of expereince
t_values <- as.data.frame(matrix(nrow = 20, ncol = 5))
colnames(t_values) <- c("Tenure", "VarianceJoint", "SEjoint", "T_statistic", "p_value")
t_values$Tenure[1:20] <- 1:20


# This is the covariance between the two (interaction) terms we want: 
covar <- vcov(discrete_model_quad)[65,66]
# Need to extract the standard errors from the key (interaction) terms in the model
summary_model <- summary(discrete_model_quad)
# This is for the gender*experience term
intx_se <- summary_model[[66,2]]
# This is for the gender*experience^2 term
intx_sq_se <- summary_model[[65,2]]


# Now compute joint variance at each level of experience:
# Formula: Var(aX + bY) = a^2 * Var(X) + b^2 * Var(Y) + 2ab * Cov(X,Y)
t_values$VarianceJoint <- 1^2 * (intx_se^2) + (2*t_values$Tenure)^2 * (intx_sq_se^2) + 2*1*2*t_values$Tenure * covar
# Now convert variance to SE
t_values$SEjoint <- sqrt(t_values$VarianceJoint)
```

```{r}
# STEPS 3 & 4
# The t-statistic should be the coefficients we are trying to test divided by the (joint) standard error of those coefficients

# Save the sample size
n <- nrow(merged_test_first_only)

t_values$T_statistic <- round((genderxtenureeffect + 2 * genderxtenure.sq.effect * t_values$Tenure) / t_values$SEjoint,2)
# Now generate the corresponding p-values (use the absolute value of the t-statistic since the sign goes both ways)
# Multiplying by 2 here to give us a 2-tailed test
t_values$p_value <- round(2*pt(abs(t_values$T_statistic), (n-1), lower.tail = FALSE),3)
t_values
```
